title: Viewing Objects: Views from the Front, Side and Top
seo_title: Grade 5 Viewing Objects Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise and match different views of the same everyday objects; identify everyday objects from different positions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 viewing objects worksheets: views from the front, side and top, matching views and counting cubes. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Draw only what you can see from that position.
key_sub: The top view does not show the height.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Objects look different from different positions.
  • The view from the top shows the squares you see looking down.
  • The view from the front shows the tallest stack in each column.
  • Some cubes can be hidden behind others.

Examples

Example

Stacks of 3, 1 and 2 cubes in a row

front view: columns 3, 1, 2

Answer: top view: 3 squares in a row

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
What you knowDraw only what you see.
Side or top?The top view looks down.
Hidden cubesCount the cubes underneath.

faq.q: Can two stacks have the same top view?
faq.a: Yes, the top view does not show the height.

items.q: How many cubes are in this structure? Every stack stands on the table.
items.e: Count stack by stack, including the cubes hidden underneath and behind: 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 13. Counting only the cubes you can see gives 10.

items.q: How many cubes are in this structure? Every stack stands on the table.
items.e: Count stack by stack, including the cubes hidden underneath and behind: 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 8. Counting only the cubes you can see gives 7.

items.q: How many cubes are in this structure? Every stack stands on the table.
items.e: Count stack by stack, including the cubes hidden underneath and behind: 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 11. Counting only the cubes you can see gives 10.

items.q: The mat plan shows how many cubes are in each stack. How many cubes are there in all?
items.e: Add the numbers on the mat plan: 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 9. 6 is only the number of stacks.

items.q: The mat plan shows how many cubes are in each stack. How many cubes are there in all?
items.e: Add the numbers on the mat plan: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 14. 8 is only the number of stacks.

items.q: These are the top, front and right side views of a structure of cubes. What is the greatest number of cubes it could have?
items.e: Make each stack as tall as both the front view (its column) and the side view (its row) allow: 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 11. The least possible is 9, so the views alone do not fix the number of cubes.

items.q: These are the top, front and right side views of a structure of cubes. What is the greatest number of cubes it could have?
items.e: Make each stack as tall as both the front view (its column) and the side view (its row) allow: 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 8. The least possible is 7, so the views alone do not fix the number of cubes.

items.q: These are the top, front and right side views of a structure of cubes. How many cubes are in the structure?
items.e: The top view shows 8 stacks. Use the front and side views to find each stack’s height: 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 12. Adding the squares in the front and side views (7 + 5) counts some cubes twice.

items.q: These are the top, front and right side views of a structure of cubes. How many cubes are in the structure?
items.e: The top view shows 8 stacks. Use the front and side views to find each stack’s height: 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11. Adding the squares in the front and side views (4 + 6) counts some cubes twice.

items.q: These are the top, front and right side views of a structure of cubes. How many cubes are in the structure?
items.e: The top view shows 4 stacks. Use the front and side views to find each stack’s height: 3 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 7. Adding the squares in the front and side views (6 + 4) counts some cubes twice.

items.q: Elna has 25 linking cubes. She builds this structure. How many cubes does she have left?
items.e: The structure has 2 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 8 cubes (count the hidden ones too). 25 − 8 = 17.

items.q: Vusi wants every stack in this mat plan to be 3 cubes tall, to make a solid rectangular prism. How many more cubes does he need?
items.e: A solid prism 3 by 2 by 3 has 3 × 2 × 3 = 18 cubes. Vusi already has 12: 18 − 12 = 6.

items.q: Precious builds this structure from 1 cm cubes. What is its volume?
items.e: Each 1 cm cube has a volume of 1 cm³. There are 2 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 9 cubes, so the volume is 9 cm³ (cubic units, not cm²).

items.q: Pieter draws the front view of this structure on grid paper, one square for each cube face. How many squares does he shade?
items.e: From the front, the tallest stacks are 3, 2 and 2 cubes, so the view has 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 squares. Cubes behind the front ones are hidden and do not add squares.
